free_tier.stated: No free tier and no free trial, stated explicitly: 'NewsDemon does not offer a free trial. We used to, but payment processing partners discourage trial-to-paid conversion flows'.

per_object_cap.notes: an article size is a protocol convention, not a vendor number

retention.stated: 5,914+ days of binary and text retention on the plans page; the block page prints 5,854++ days. The conservative figure is recorded.

egress.terms: Unlimited speed and downloads on the unlimited plans; 50 SSL connections on every plan

interface_detail: NNTP over TLS on port 563; no HTTP or object API exists for the download path, so a user drives it through SABnzbd, NZBGet or nzbdav
tooling: SABnzbd, NZBGet or nzbdav over NNTP/TLS; any newsreader works because the protocol is the same everywhere, and no provider SDK is needed
chaining: The usual shape is a NewsDemon unlimited primary plus an Abavia block as fill: two independent spools, one subscription and one prepaid allowance.

limits.value: 50 SSL connections on every plan, including the $3 metered tier
50 GB/month on the metered tier; blocks of 100 GB, 500 GB and 1 TB never expire
5,854 to 5,914 days depending on the page

limits_note: Three unlimited terms (monthly, quarterly, annual) plus metered 50/100/200 GB and non-expiring blocks. Blocks are listed twice on the same page at two price columns: 100 GB at $15 or $17, 500 GB at $47 or $49, 1000 GB at $87 or $89. A separate page offers a 100 GB block for $5 and a 50 GB metered plan for $3/mo.
binding_note: The annual unlimited plan publishes no byte counter. At 1 TiB/month nothing in the vocabulary binds on that tier; the metered tier would bind at 50 GB by construction.

identity_cost.detail: No trial at all, so a card or another accepted payment is required before the first byte. The vendor does not publish its payment list on the pages read; crypto is reported by the r/usenet deals wiki and was not confirmed here.

reliability_note: UsenetExpress backbone with NewsDemon's own spool on top, three regions (US East, US West, EU), 550 TB/day feed claimed. Post-quantum encryption is advertised on every plan.
confidence_note: All prices and the explicit refusal of a free trial come from vendor pages read. The two block price columns disagree with each other on the same page and the record keeps the higher.

evidence.proved: unlimited monthly/quarterly/annual plus 50/100/200 GB metered and 100 GB/500 GB/1 TB blocks; 50 SSL connections; 5,914+ days
'NewsDemon does not offer a free trial'; 50 GB metered at $3/mo, 100 GB block at $5, unlimited annual at $60/yr

notes: The $3 metered plan is the cheapest paid entry of any provider and carries the same 50 connections as the unlimited plans.

extras.crypto: reported by r/usenet wiki/providerdeals, not vendor-confirmed
